analysis: Reviewed the BASE excerpts of ClusterService.swift (base lines 911-1536) against the head patch summary. The changes are confined to update handling and status reporting. Head 107-108 adds the updateWaitLine state. Head 943 sets the status field pairUpdate from ClusterPairUpdate.readProgress(updateProgressPath(serviceDirectory: store.paths.directory)). Head 974-984 and 989 add a guard inside checkForUpdate: if the pinned and current worker digests do not come from a single build (ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild), the service logs a wait line once and returns without stopping parts or re-planning. This replaces the base say at base 975-976. Security effect: the guard only defers an automatic stop/plan/adopt/serve while the two Macs report different builds. The base comment at 983-986 says both Macs already refuse parts whose worker digest no longer matches the saved pin, so deferring re-adoption fails closed for serving. It does not admit a mismatched build, so no new authorization or attestation path relevant to TB-011, T-054 or A-017 is visible. The peer's runtimeBinarySHA256 (base 968) is self-reported over the cluster link and was already used to decide the update before this PR. A peer that misreports its digest can keep the leader waiting, a local availability issue for an operator-controlled pair rather than a new cross-tenant risk. The pairUpdate progress file is local service-directory state. Its contents and permissions are not visible here: ClusterPairUpdate.readProgress and ClusterServiceAgent.updateProgressPath are not supplied. Integration should confirm the parser bounds its input size and that the file is owner-only. The status JSON is published to service-status.json (base 1187-1191) and may be relayed to the peer via the status op (base 1064). Prefix-cache handling (cacheSync, reclaim at base 935 and 1365-1369; T-041) and the approval and stop paths are unchanged. No regression identified.
